groups.title: Server-Side Rendering
groups.question: Your Astro site needs a server-rendered account page and must deploy to Netlify. Explain adapters and how pages read the request.

followUps.SSR Adapters: Why does server rendering need an adapter?
followUps.Request and Response Objects: How does a server-rendered page read headers and cookies?

evidence.text: An adapter builds the server output for a specific runtime.
There are adapters for Node, Netlify, Vercel and others.
Without one, server-rendered pages cannot be deployed.
Astro.request gives the standard Request object.
It provides headers, URL and other request data.
Request data is only meaningful in server-rendered pages, not static ones.

notEnough: Only saying you read the request.

groups.title: API Endpoints
groups.question: You need a JSON endpoint for a newsletter signup and a check on every request for logged-in users. Explain endpoints and middleware in Astro.

followUps.REST Endpoints in src/pages: How do you create an API endpoint in Astro?
followUps.Middleware in Astro: What does middleware do in Astro?

evidence.text: A .ts file in src/pages exports functions named after HTTP methods.
Each returns a Response object.
Endpoints that handle POST need server rendering.

notEnough: Only saying you add a .ts file.

evidence.text: Middleware runs before every request.
It is defined with onRequest in src/middleware.ts.
It suits authentication, logging and adding data to locals.

groups.title: Node.js Integration
groups.question: Your server-rendered pages are slow to show anything, and a developer used a secret API key in client code. Explain the Node adapter's streaming and environment variables.

followUps.Node.js Adapter and Streaming: How does streaming improve server-rendered pages?
followUps.Environment Variables and Secrets: How does Astro keep secrets out of the browser?

evidence.text: The Node adapter runs Astro as a Node server.
It streams HTML as it is generated.
Users see the first content sooner instead of waiting for the whole page.
Only variables with the PUBLIC_ prefix are exposed to the browser.
Others are server-only.
Secrets must never get the PUBLIC_ prefix.

notEnough: Only saying you use env vars.

groups.title: Cookies and Sessions
groups.question: You are adding login to a server-rendered Astro site. Explain how cookies and sessions should work.

followUps.Cookie API in Astro SSR: What does Astro.cookies give you over raw headers?
followUps.Authentication Patterns: How would authentication work across requests?

evidence.text: Astro.cookies reads and sets cookies in pages and endpoints.
It lets you set options like HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.
It is less error-prone than building Set-Cookie headers by hand.
A session token is stored in an HttpOnly cookie.
Middleware validates it on every request.
The user is put on Astro.locals for pages and endpoints to use.

notEnough: Only saying you check the cookie.
